thinkingMap.title: Tool for tracking reading
thinkingMap.seedIdea: I want to build something that helps me keep track of what I read, but every app I've tried I abandon after a week.

message.content: I want to build something that helps me keep track of what I read, but every app I've tried I abandon after a week.
The abandonment is the interesting part, not the tracking. Before we design anything: what were you actually hoping to get out of the record, and what made logging feel like a chore?
Honestly I wanted to be able to find a half-remembered idea again months later. The logging itself never gave me anything back.

mapNode.label: Abandoned after a week
mapNode.detail: Every existing reading tracker has been dropped within days. The tracking is not the problem to solve — the abandonment is.

mapNode.label: Refind a half-remembered idea
mapNode.detail: Contributed by the person directly: the point of the record is retrieval months later, not the log itself.

mapNode.label: Logging gives nothing back
mapNode.detail: The loop never closes: you put entries in and the tool never hands you anything for having done so.

mapNode.label: Capture the thought, not the book
mapNode.detail: Record the sentence that struck you rather than the title and the page count — retrieval works on ideas, not metadata.

mapNode.label: Do you reread your own notes today?
Is this for you alone, or shared?
